$comment: Machine-readable index of Open Psychology Interactives.
This file is the single source of truth for what has been published.
When you add an interactive, append an entry to the matching collection's
'interactives' array; assets/js/main.js renders those entries onto the
collection pages. While an array is empty the page keeps its static
'in preparation' message, so the site never claims a tool exists before
it does. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the field-by-field description.

project.name: Open Psychology Interactives
project.description: Free, accessible, classroom-ready browser-based teaching tools for statistics, personality and individual differences, and neuropsychology.

collections.title: Statistics
collections.summary: Interactives for the inferential ideas that students most often meet as formulae first and intuition second: sampling variation, uncertainty, and what a test statistic is actually responding to.

plannedTopics.title: Sampling distributions
plannedTopics.detail: Repeatedly drawing samples from a known population and watching the distribution of the sample mean take shape.

plannedTopics.title: Confidence intervals
plannedTopics.detail: What the interval covers across repeated samples, and what it does not say about a single study.

plannedTopics.title: p-values and significance testing
plannedTopics.detail: How a p-value responds to effect size, sample size and variability, held apart one at a time.

plannedTopics.title: Correlation and regression
plannedTopics.detail: Building a scatterplot point by point to see how outliers, range restriction and non-linearity move the coefficient.

plannedTopics.title: Statistical power
plannedTopics.detail: The trade-off between sample size, effect size and the chance of detecting a real effect.

collections.title: Personality and Individual Differences
collections.summary: Interactives for trait structure and psychological measurement: where factors come from, what reliability and validity buy you, and why profiles are harder to interpret than they look.

plannedTopics.title: Trait structure and the Big Five
plannedTopics.detail: How correlations between many items resolve into a small number of broad dimensions.

plannedTopics.title: Factor analysis, made visible
plannedTopics.detail: Watching a correlation matrix reduce to factors, and seeing how the number retained changes the story.

plannedTopics.title: Reliability
plannedTopics.detail: How internal consistency and test–retest reliability respond to scale length and item quality.

plannedTopics.title: Validity and measurement error
plannedTopics.detail: Why an unreliable measure limits the correlation it can show with anything else.

plannedTopics.title: Reading a trait profile
plannedTopics.detail: Norms, percentiles and standard error of measurement, and the width of the band around a single score.

collections.title: Neuropsychology
collections.summary: Interactives for brain–behaviour reasoning and the classic experimental tasks, so students can experience the paradigm before they read the effect size.

plannedTopics.title: Classic attention tasks
plannedTopics.detail: Runnable versions of Stroop-type and cueing paradigms, with the student's own data shown afterwards.

plannedTopics.title: Working memory and span
plannedTopics.detail: Span procedures that make the capacity limit something a student meets rather than reads about.

plannedTopics.title: Dissociation logic
plannedTopics.detail: Single and double dissociations, and what each licenses you to conclude about separable processes.

plannedTopics.title: Executive function
plannedTopics.detail: Set-shifting and inhibition tasks, with the switch cost calculated from the student's own responses.

plannedTopics.title: Interpreting deficits
plannedTopics.detail: Why performance on a task rarely maps onto one region, and how case evidence accumulates.
